in Scheme 5, the formal synthesis of bioactive compounds or
natural products was conducted using the current method as a
key step. As an example, endocannabinoid probe 17, an
anandamide (AEA) analogue with exceptional CB1 receptor
afinity, was synthesized using compound 15 as a key
intermediate. The synthesis commenced with an asymmetric
alkynylation of the

provided skipped diyne 12. Subsequent sequential desilylation
and cross-coupling converted 13 into the corresponding
tetrayne 14. Finally, a selective semihydrogenation aforded
the skipped tetraene, delivering probe 15 in 22% overall yield
and 90% ee of 4 steps, which is much more eficient than the
reported method from compound 16 with 12 steps, even in a
similar overall yield.<sup>5a</sup> Second, the synthesis of sex pheromone

Scheme 5. Synthetic Applications
In summary, we have developed a copper-catalyzed
asymmetric alkynylation of
s p ^ { 2 } \mathrm { C - } \dot { \mathrm { H } }
bonds in silyl-substituted
allenes. This method provides eficient access to chiral skipped
diynes in high yields with excellent enantioselectivities. The
method features a broad substrate scope and robust functional
group tolerance, accommodating both alkynyl silanes and
boronic esters. Moreover, the resulting skipped diynes serve as
versatile key synthons for incorporating enantiomerically
enriched enynes, alkynes, alkanes, and their derivatives, which
could be applied in the concise synthesis of several bioactive
molecules.
